subject: Re: [stan-users] How to pass an int matrix into a user-defined function?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to pass an int matrix into a user-defined function?
parts:
There are no integer matrices in Stan. Only integer two-dimensional
arrays. You can put integers into a matrix[M, N], but you can't
get them out as integers, only as real values.

- Bob

> On Aug 24, 2016, at 8:48 PM, Lu Zhang <ny...@g.ucla.edu> wrote:
>
>
> I need to pass an integer matrix for indicating the index of the nearest neighborhood. I pass the matrix as
> int[,] nearind,
>
> and use it in a for-loop
> for (i in 2:N){
> ...
> for (j in 1:dim){
>
> k = nearind[(i-1),j];
>
> Uw[i] = Uw[i] - u[j] * w[k];
>
> }
>
> }
>
> But I got this error when running in R
> SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:
>
> unknown variable in assignment; lhs variable=k
>
> ERROR at line 46

> 44: v2 = mdivide_right_tri_low(v', L);
